newsitem.title: INDIA: India gilts up on hopes of falling interest rates.
newsitem.headline: India gilts up on hopes of falling interest rates.

text.p: Prices of Indian government securities firmed up in active trade on Thursday fuelled by easy call money and expectations of lower interest rates in the future, dealers said.
They said several banks were building positions as they anticipated a fall in interest rates after the Reserve Bank of India unveils its credit policy in April.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram asked banks to cut interest rates and boost the flow of funds to industry earlier this week.
Dealers said prices of securities moved up across maturities but most of the demand was for medium-term stocks.

The 12 percent 1999 stock traded on Thursday at 100.08 rupees against its last traded 100.02, the 13.50 percent 1997 at 101.45 against 101.40 and the 13.50 percent 1998 at 103.15 against 103.10, dealers said.
Other stocks which traded higher included the 13.82 percent 2002 which moved up to 101.94 from 101.75 and the zero-coupon 2000 at 65.43 rupees against 65.38.
Call money eased on reduced demand to end Thursday at 4.5 percent, down from opening quotes of 4.75-5.25 percent, dealers said.
They said most of the day's business was between 4.75 and 5.0 percent with stray deals at 4.0 percent.
Dealers said fears of advance tax payments leading to a tightening in call money rates had proved to be unfounded.
Advance tax payments by companies were expected to flow from banks into government coffers from Thursday. Analysts had estimated the outflows between 30 billion and 50 billion rupees.
"So far there has been no impact from tax outflows," said a dealer at a private bank.
"I think the market may have discounted the outflows already. We will know over the next couple of days," he said.
